supportedContent.dmgThroughCgbRgb555Palette: supported when Gambatte colorization is explicitly GBC and the resulting raster obeys this contract
supportedContent.gbaEnhancedCgbMode: out-of-scope in v1; gambatte_gb_hwmode must remain Auto rather than GBA

timeSemantics.monotonic: Temporal integration requires strictly increasing committed CGB frame identifiers; wall-clock timestamps alone are insufficient.
timeSemantics.ordinaryFrame: Update temporal state exactly once for each committed core frame at 70224 / 4194304 seconds.
timeSemantics.pause: Freeze all ordinary-response and retention state; do not integrate elapsed wall time.
timeSemantics.reset: Discard ordinary-response and retention history, then seed from the first complete post-reset RGB555 frame with zero elapsed exposure.
timeSemantics.contentLoad: Discard all prior-content state, then seed from the first complete new-content RGB555 frame with zero elapsed exposure.
timeSemantics.saveStateLoad: Treat as a discontinuity: discard temporal and retention history, seed the loaded frame statically, and resume only from a new monotonic frame baseline.
timeSemantics.focusLoss: If emulation pauses, freeze state. If emulation continues but presentation frames are not delivered one-for-one, enter static bypass until a reset baseline is established.
timeSemantics.fastForward: Supported only when every emulated CGB frame is delivered once in order. Frame dropping, coalescing, or wall-time scaling enters static bypass.
timeSemantics.rewind: Reverse-time integration is forbidden. Every rewind discontinuity clears state and presents the current source through the static color path.
timeSemantics.runAhead: Only the committed final frame may update state; speculative frames must never reach the reconstruction. Otherwise enter static bypass.
timeSemantics.subframe: Unsupported in reference-v1 because multiple host updates for one CGB frame would invent drive events; enter static bypass.
timeSemantics.failurePolicy: Fail closed to the current-frame static WS1 color path with temporal response and retention disabled; never guess elapsed frames or integrate backward. A core-option mismatch refuses reference-preset activation entirely.
